title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study multiplicative structures on 'half-simplicial' (semi-simplicial, i.e. without degeneracies) ∂-perfect complexes. K is a k-linear category of standard simplex cochain complexes, essentially the complexes ΛΦ^* attached to the simplices C^i. It carries a join operation *, with Δ^i * Δ^j = Δ^{i+j+1}. A coefficient object F: K → B is a family C^i = F(C^i) in an abelian (tensor) category B, with differentials d^i: C^i → C^{i+1} coming from the semi-simplicial structure. Its 'realization' is C^* = DP^*(C), a total-complex construction.

Previous page. A multiplicative structure is meant to be a lax-monoidal structure F(X) ⊗_B F(Y) → F(X*Y) with respect to the join. Unwinding this gives maps
u_ij: (C^i ⊗_B C^j) ⊗_k C^*_ij → C^*, where C^*_ij = ΛΦ^* ⊗ ΛΦ^* is the dual of the join complex C_i * C_j.

This page, first part. It states the compatibilities these maps must satisfy:
- for fixed (i,j), compatibility with the semi-simplicial structure of C^*_ij;
- for varying (i,j), compatibility with the differentials ('q. diff', reading uncertain), written as a commutative square. Starting from (C^i⊗C^j)⊗C^{*n}_{(i+1)j}, one can map either by 1⊗1⊗d^{*n}_{(i+1)j} to (C^i⊗C^j)⊗C^{*n}_{ij} and then by u_ij to C^*, or by d^i⊗1⊗1 to (C^{i+1}⊗C^j)⊗C^{*n}_{(i+1)j} and then by u_{(i+1)j} to C^*. The two composites must agree.
In modern terms the u_ij form an extranatural (dinatural) family. That is, they give a map out of the coend ∫^{i,j} (C^i⊗C^j)⊗C^*_ij, i.e. a weighted-colimit/realization compatibility.
He adds that unit, associativity and commutativity data are also required, and that these will need to be made explicit in a particularly careful way.

This page, the Remark. K has no unit for * (the empty simplex is not in K). So unit compatibility cannot be stated inside K. Proposed remedy: enlarge K to categories P_0 or Q = P_1, which contain a unit object 1 and carry a class Σ of distinguished short exact sequences. Then additive functors Q → B (resp. P_0 → B) that are Σ-left exact, i.e. send Σ-short exact sequences 0→A'→A→A''→0 to exact sequences 0→F(A')→F(A)→F(A''), should correspond via F ↦ F(1) (plus complementary data) to certain complexes in B satisfying conditions.

Next page. This is developed further: Σ-cartesian functors P → B correspond to complexes C^i → C^{i+1} with conditions on cycles, using Σ-resolutions of each L ∈ P by objects of K.

Purpose. In effect this replaces the non-unital semi-simplicial join category by an augmented/unital envelope. There, monoidal structure and units make sense, and functors on the envelope are recovered from their restriction to K by exactness.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The page is programmatic: the unit/assoc/comm compatibilities are announced but not written out.
The characterization of Σ-left-exact functors via F ↦ F(1) is left incomplete at the bottom of the page; the conditions on the target data are illegible or unfinished.
The square only shows the i-direction differential; the analogous j-direction square, with its Koszul sign, is implicit.

ideas.what: Multiplicative structure on a semi-simplicial coefficient system as lax-monoidal data w.r.t. join, encoded by maps (C^i⊗C^j)⊗C^*_ij → C^* subject to a dinaturality square
ideas.modern_name: Lax monoidal functor for Day convolution / ordinal sum (join); extranatural transformation out of a coend (weighted realization); cup products on totalizations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Day (convolution, 1970); Kelly/Street (ends, dinaturality); Alexander–Whitney/Eilenberg–Zilber for products on cochains

ideas.what: Observation that the semi-simplicial join category is non-unital, so units must be handled by passing to an augmented/unital envelope (P_0, Q)
ideas.modern_name: Semi-simplicial (Δ_inj) vs augmented Δ_inj,+ with ordinal sum: the latter is the free monoidal category on a pointed object; units in semi-simplicial/A∞ settings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; for semi-simplicial units cf. Lurie, Steimle and others (2000s–2010s)

ideas.what: Additive Σ-left-exact functors from an exact-type category Q or P_0 to B are determined by their value on the unit plus complementary data (a complex in B)
ideas.modern_name: Eilenberg–Watts / Gabriel–Popescu-type representation of left exact functors; left Kan extension from a generating subcategory with resolutions

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags the need to define unit, associativity and commutativity constraints for join-multiplicative semi-simplicial ∂-perfect complexes, and to fix the non-unitality of K via an exact-category envelope. The program is only sketched here. The specific 'dévissage + multiplicative' framework does not seem to have been written up anywhere, though the underlying ideas are now standard in other guises (Day convolution, E∞-structures on totalizations).
missed.quote: K n'a pas d'unité pour * ! donc on ne exprimer directement, en restant dans K, une compatibilité avec les unités! Comment s'en tirer?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly of historical interest: an early attempt (c. 1975) at coherent multiplicative structures on non-unital semi-simplicial data, a problem later solved by ∞-categorical methods.

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but standard-in-hindsight coherence considerations (dinaturality of a product with respect to the join; units requiring an augmented envelope). They are historically nice as early thinking about non-unital semi-simplicial monoidal structure, but contain no result absent from the modern literature.
transcription_corrections: The first line likely reads 'homs compatibles avec str. ½ simpl. (pour i,j fixés) et avec q. diff (pour i,j variables)'; the first word is probably 'homs'.
The right vertical arrow of the square is labelled 'd^i ⊗ − ⊗ −'. The bottom-left target is C^* (the realization), not a struck-out expression; the crossed-out word there is illegible.
'Ce demandera' is probably 'Ceci demandera'. The illegible adjective after 'particulièrement' may be 'précise' (uncertain).
In the last lines, 'correspondent ... F ↦ F(1)' probably reads 'correspondent par F ↦ F(1) aux complexes ... dans B tels que ...' (uncertain).
